About the Role

We are seeking a qualified capital/finance professional to lead the capital and control workstream for new regulated insurance entities established by the Group — including DFSA, Cayman and Lloyd’s structures. The primary focus is on new entity establishment: defining the capital structure, building the financial control framework, and establishing the regulatory reporting infrastructure from inception. Once entities are operational, you will support their ongoing financial and regulatory requirements, alongside existing entities and reinsurance programmes. You will also supervise a junior analyst. This is a build‑focused role for someone comfortable standing things up from scratch, not just running steady‑state reporting.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the financial establishment of new regulated entities (DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s and others) – defining the opening balance sheet, capital structure and financial control framework from inception, ensuring each entity is correctly capitalised and controlled before it writes business.
  • Build capital adequacy and solvency models for each new entity to meet regulator requirements; maintain and update these models as the entity grows.
  • Establish the regulatory reporting framework for each new jurisdiction (e.g., DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s), including designing the reporting pack, setting the reporting calendar and producing the first returns; hand over to ongoing support once embedded.
  • Build the financial model for each new entity – three‑statement model and entity‑level profit and loss – establishing the management reporting suite for ongoing reporting.
  • Establish the reinsurance programme accounting structure for new entities (quota share, excess of loss, ceding commission), ensuring correct accounting treatment and control framework from inception; support existing programmes as required.
  • Produce the first monthly management accounts and entity‑level reporting pack for each new entity, establishing format, commentary structure and distribution; support ongoing production for existing entities as required.
  • Reconcile intercompany balances and positions across group entities.
  • Manage the Group’s Funds at Lloyd’s (FAL) position for the Syndicate in a Box (SIAB) – providing feeds to C&C’s selected managing agent for the annual capital setting process, optimising FAL composition across cash, LOCs and approved investments, responding to Lloyd’s capital calls, and maintaining FAL headroom analysis relative to approved capital requirement.
  • Run capital adequacy stress testing and scenario analysis across the Group’s regulated entities – including shock loss, premium volume growth and FX sensitivity – to assess headroom above SCR/MCR thresholds and inform capital deployment decisions.
  • Manage collateral arrangements supporting the Group’s reinsurance programmes – letters of credit, trust accounts and cash deposits – ensuring collateral is correctly sized, documented and renewed per programme terms and regulatory requirements.
  • Own the capital waterfall and inter‑entity funding mechanics – managing dividend upstream, shareholder loan repayment and capital repatriation between regulated entities and the parent, ensuring all movements are within approved limits and correctly documented.
  • Track and report reinsurance counterparty credit exposure across the Group’s programmes, maintaining the counterparty register and flagging rating changes, concentration risk or collateral shortfalls.
  • Produce the board‑level capital reporting pack – including capital dashboard, solvency headroom by entity, FAL position and stress test outcomes – on a quarterly basis or as required by the board or managing agent.
  • Support existing entities and reinsurance programmes as required, covering financial control, reporting or capital queries where capacity or expertise is needed.
  • Supervise and direct the Capital & Structuring Analyst on day‑to‑day work.
